title: AMIV General Assembly
markdown:
The AMIV board cordially invites you to the general assembly for FS19.

title: From nanotech to living sensors: unraveling the spin physics of biosensing at the nanoscale
markdown:
The Quantum Engineering Commission is pleased
to announce that Clarice D. Aiello will be giving a
talk on Biosensing and Quantum Engineering. She
is an expert on nanosensors harnessing roomtemperature
quantum effects in noisy
environments. Aiello received her Ph.D. from MIT
in Electrical Engineering and held postdoctoral
appointments in Bioengineering at Stanford, and in
Chemistry at Berkeley. She joined UCLA in 2019,
where she leads the Quantum Biology Tech
(QuBiT) Lab.

title: Fire and Flämmli
markdown:
New to swiss culture or just on the lookout for some fiery action after months of distancing? Release your inner arsonist with Switzerland’s favourite pyrotechnic refreshment. For the uninitiated: a “Flämmli” is an exciting cocktail consisting of coffee, a smattering of caramelised sugar and, most importantly, a flaming dash of ignited alcohol. While we can’t teach you how to take proper pictures of your blistering brew, this event will show you everything else! Since this drink is a rare indulgence, AMIV will even be helping you finance your 1L bottle of spirit, so that it’ll be the alcohol, not the price, burning holes in your pockets. May you use your newfound knowledge to impress flat mates and family alike!

Make sure you stock your home with coffee, and prepare your finest mug and heroin spoon a sturdy spoon, as well as some backups in case things get steamy ;)

IMPORTANT: You must choose one of the options below by writing "Yes" or "No"! While you can, in practice, “flämmel” with any alcohol over 40% abv, the classic sweet and fruity notes of Williams and other similar Kernobst-Schnapps are truly irreplaceable. If you happen to already have a bottle at home, you’re in luck, as the event is free! (editors note: buy the financed bottle even if you already have one, and flämmel to your heart’s content for weeks on end!)

title: blitz looking for members
markdown:
Write an article for the blitz (topic: DACH), get invited to the next meeting and get a pizza for free.

The 12th May 2021 is the last editorial deadline of the blitz. We are looking for new members and sadly we cannot convince you of the groundbreaking advantages in a split second next to the beer vending machine in the common room. That's why we pulled out a classic: you write an article for the blitz, we get you a pizza delivered to your home. But the article has to pass our quality check. As for a non-german speaker we can't just tell you to "read the blitz" to understand what "quality" means, so just be confident in your writing.

The next, and last, blitz topic this semester is DACH, an apronym for the countries Germany, Austria and Switzerland, maybe that helps with the inspiration for an article? Your idea doesn't fit? Doesn't matter, usually most articles in an issue do not fit the topic printed on it. So get infront of your keyboard and send your article to artikel@blitz.ethz.ch!

You do not like to write, but still want to maybe have lunch every second week in a Corona-free semester? Then write us at info@blitz.ethz.ch and we can look together, if we find something for you to do in the blitz.

title: Bühler Group Excursion
markdown:
Bühler Group is a global technology company that strives to create innovations for a better world, with a special focus on healthy, safe, and sustainable solutions. Every day, billions of people come into contact with our technologies to cover their basic needs for food and mobility, and more.
 
Want to get to know us and some of our amazing STEM women? We from Generation B - an employee-led change-making movement within Bühler - invite LIMES students to our CUBIC Innovation Campus to introduce you to Bühler technologies and people! The event will take place on May 18 and will include an introduction to Bühler and Generation B, a tour of our innovative Campus, as well as a networking apero where you can exchange with some of our amazing female engineers and scientists.
The maximum number of participants is 10, and within our premises in Uzwil, we're adhering to strict safety measures to keep you and everyone at Bühler safe.
Sign up for this opportunity now! We from Bühler and Generation B are excited to get to know you.
Meeting point: Zurich main station (under the big clock in the main hall) at 13:30

markdown:
Developing machine learning technologies in real-world applications continues to challenge many organizations. Additionally, developing skills in this area can be difficult due to limited real-world data and use cases available in academia. One way to address this is by writing smart AI solutions using real-world data and use cases. Picnic (https://picnic.app/de/), an online supermarket scale-up, is offering a hackathon with real-life data to challenge and help students build up their knowledge in data science, software engineering, and strategy. 
In Part 1 of this event, we'll introduce the case and the data.  🧠
In Part 2, we will run a hackathon around payments, fraud and transparency in which data science meets software engineering and strategy! 💻
In Part 3, you will present your results in front of a jury for the chance to win amazing SWAGS! But no worries, we will have surprising gadgets for everyone! ✨
Over the whole day, we will provide snacks and a short lunch break with pizza and drinks. Experts will support you with all of your questions over the day. 
After the hackathon, you will have the opportunity to listen to our speakers, chat with them and network with other Google DSC members around a free aperitif (limited spots available, please make sure to also sign-up for our second event, if interested)! 🍸🍕
Please sign-up here for the hackathon (limited spots available).

title: AI with Picnic: Speaker sessions

title: AMIV goes Opera
markdown:
Participation in the event is free of charge. HOWEVER, A CLUB JUNG-MEMBERSHIP at the Zurich Opera House (one-time fee of CHF 20.-) is required.

Registration: https://www.opernhaus.ch/jung/club-jung/

In Erich Wolfgang Korngold's opera Die tote Stadt, the story revolves around a young man named Paul, whose beloved wife Marie passed away at an early age. Paul retreats into solitude, completely consumed by his grief, until one day, Marietta appears—a woman who strongly resembles Marie. Paul becomes infatuated with Marietta, as she rekindles long-suppressed desires within him, leading to an obsession. However, he simultaneously struggles with feelings of guilt and betrayal towards his deceased wife. As Marietta begins to claim more space in his life and rebels against the constant presence of the dead, Paul kills her. But soon after, he starts to question himself—did he really kill Marietta? Why does she suddenly seem to be alive again? Can he still trust his own perception?

First performed in 1920, Korngold's third opera struck a deep chord with audiences of its time, as evidenced by the overwhelming success of its simultaneous premieres in Cologne and Hamburg. After World War II, Korngold—who had emigrated to the United States due to his Jewish heritage and became known for his Hollywood film scores—fell into relative obscurity. However, since the 1970s, his works have been rediscovered to great acclaim on both German and international stages.

With this production, Dmitri Tcherniakov returns to the Zurich Opera House. He previously opened the first season under Andreas Homoki’s directorship and has since staged operas worldwide. In Zurich, he has already brought Jenůfa (2012), Pelléas et Mélisande, and The Makropulos Case to the stage. Now, with his signature sensitivity and psychological depth, he takes on Die tote Stadt. The Swiss conductor Lorenzo Viotti, currently General Music Director of the Dutch National Opera in Amsterdam, will bring Korngold’s vibrant orchestral colors to life. The demanding yet highly rewarding lead roles will be performed by Vida Miknevičiũte and Eric Cutler.

title: Against an increase in tuition fees
markdown:
On October 1st 2025, we will meet at 12:30 p.m. at Helvetiaplatz, walk together with posters and banners to Zurich HB and then travel to the demonstration in Bern at the Bundesplatz. There, our Swiss umbrella organisation (VSS) is organising a large demonstration against the planned increase in tuition fees. We will be offering day tickets for 5 CHF for a train there and a train back. 

As part of saving budget for the year 2027, the Federal Council plans to massively raise tuition fees for all Swiss universities – specifically a doubling for Swiss students and a quadrupling for foreign students. This would exclude many students and make higher education unaffordable.
Join us on the streets. Together we will show that education must not be a luxury.

More info: bezahlbar-studieren.ch
